You are a senior frontend engineer, Chrome Extension engineer, and product UI/UX designer.

I already have an existing Chrome extension with working functionality. I now want you to EXTEND it — not rewrite it from scratch — by adding a complete UI enhancement layer specifically for the COMSATS Lahore Student Information System:

https://lhr-sis.comsats.edu.pk

The goal is to transform the existing SIS experience into a much more modern, polished, readable, useful student dashboard while preserving 100% of the portal's original functionality.

IMPORTANT:
- First inspect and understand my existing extension architecture.
- Do not remove, break, or unnecessarily rewrite existing functionality.
- Integrate this feature cleanly into the current extension.
- Inspect the actual SIS DOM, routes/pages, tables, navigation and components before deciding selectors or implementation details.
- Do not assume DOM selectors without verifying them.
- The extension should progressively enhance the existing portal rather than attempting to replace the actual SIS backend/application.

# PRIMARY GOAL

Turn the old/dated SIS interface into a modern student-focused experience by providing:

1. Complete visual reskin
2. High-quality dark mode
3. Improved typography and spacing
4. Better navigation
5. Cleaner tables/forms
6. Better information hierarchy
7. Useful student dashboard summaries
8. Reorganization of existing information where it genuinely improves usability
9. Quality-of-life features that make SIS easier and faster to use

This should feel like:

"COMSATS SIS, if it had received a modern professional redesign."

NOT:

"A completely different application placed on top of SIS."

The original functionality and data remain authoritative.

# FIRST: AUDIT BEFORE IMPLEMENTING

Before changing code:

1. Inspect the existing Chrome extension.
2. Understand:
   - manifest version
   - content scripts
   - background/service worker
   - popup/side panel if present
   - storage system
   - current permissions
   - existing injected styles/scripts
   - existing functionality
   - architecture/framework
3. Inspect the SIS website while authenticated.
4. Identify:
   - dashboard/home
   - sidebar/navbar
   - student profile information
   - attendance
   - timetable
   - courses
   - grades/results
   - transcript/CGPA if available
   - fee information
   - registration
   - notices
   - forms
   - buttons
   - tables
   - modals
   - alerts
   - breadcrumbs
   - pagination
   - any other important student-facing areas
5. Determine whether SIS behaves as:
   - traditional multi-page application
   - SPA
   - partial AJAX application
   - mixture of these
6. Identify elements that can safely be visually changed versus elements whose structure should remain untouched.

Then implement the enhancement.

Do NOT stop after the audit. Continue through implementation.

# DESIGN DIRECTION

Create a professional university dashboard aesthetic.

Style characteristics:

- modern
- minimal
- clean
- polished
- highly readable
- slightly premium
- student-focused
- restrained rather than flashy
- excellent dark mode
- excellent information density
- consistent visual hierarchy

Avoid:
- excessive gradients
- excessive glassmorphism
- huge border radiuses everywhere
- neon gamer aesthetics
- unnecessary animations
- excessive shadows
- overly large UI elements
- changing the portal so aggressively that it becomes unfamiliar

Think modern products such as Linear, Notion, Vercel, modern admin dashboards and polished university portals — while retaining SIS's identity.

# DESIGN SYSTEM

Build the styling around reusable CSS variables/tokens rather than scattered hard-coded values.

For example:

--sis-bg
--sis-surface
--sis-surface-secondary
--sis-border
--sis-text
--sis-text-muted
--sis-primary
--sis-success
--sis-warning
--sis-danger
--sis-radius-sm
--sis-radius-md
--sis-shadow
--sis-spacing-*

Support both:

LIGHT MODE
and
DARK MODE

Dark mode must be intentionally designed, not simply:

filter: invert()

Use proper dark surfaces, borders, text contrast, table styling, inputs, dropdowns, modals, tooltips and hover states.

# DARK MODE

Add an extension-controlled theme system:

- Light
- Dark
- System

Persist preference using the extension's existing storage system or chrome.storage.

Dark mode should apply consistently to:

- page background
- navigation
- cards
- tables
- forms
- dropdowns
- buttons
- links
- alerts
- modals
- pagination
- tooltips
- profile areas
- headings
- secondary text
- borders
- hover states
- selected states

Do not leave random bright white components inside dark mode.

Also ensure contrast remains accessible.

# TYPOGRAPHY

Improve the existing typography considerably.

Use a modern UI font if the extension already has one available, otherwise use a safe, performant font strategy.

Create hierarchy for:

- page title
- section heading
- card title
- body
- secondary information
- metadata
- labels
- table headings

Do not make everything bold.

Improve:
- line height
- font sizing
- spacing
- alignment

# NAVIGATION

Improve the existing SIS navigation without breaking its URLs or click behavior.

Potential improvements:

- cleaner sidebar
- consistent icons where appropriate
- better active-page indication
- better grouping of related sections
- improved spacing
- clearer section names where safe
- sticky navigation if appropriate
- collapse behavior if useful
- mobile/narrow-screen behavior if relevant

If reorganizing navigation, keep all original destinations intact.

Do not create fake routes.

# DASHBOARD ENHANCEMENT

The home/dashboard should become the most useful part of the enhancement.

Where the existing SIS data allows it, create compact overview cards such as:

- current semester
- registered courses
- CGPA
- semester GPA
- attendance overview
- today's classes
- upcoming classes
- fee status
- notices
- academic warnings

ONLY display information that actually exists in SIS.

Do not fabricate data.

The dashboard may reorganize existing information from the DOM into a better presentation.

For example:

Current Semester
Fall 2026

CGPA
3.42

Courses
6 Registered

Attendance
87% Overall

Today's Classes
--------------------------------
09:00  Machine Learning
11:30  Operating Systems

But these cards must be driven by actual SIS data.

# ATTENDANCE

If SIS exposes attendance information, make this section significantly easier to understand.

Improve the existing attendance table visually.

Where mathematically safe and supported by available data, optionally show:

- attendance percentage
- attended lectures
- total lectures
- absent lectures
- progress bar
- status indicator

Use restrained semantic indicators for:

safe / warning / critical

Do not make assumptions about university attendance policy unless that policy is explicitly present in SIS.

If a minimum attendance threshold is explicitly available, you may use it.

# TIMETABLE

If a timetable exists:

Improve it into a clearer weekly schedule.

Make it easy to identify:

- course
- time
- room
- teacher if available
- current day

Highlight today's classes subtly.

Do not modify the underlying timetable data.

# RESULTS / GRADES

Improve readability of:

- semester result tables
- GPA
- CGPA
- course grades
- credit hours

Use clear hierarchy and spacing.

Potential presentation:

Course | Credits | Grade | Points

Make summary values visually prominent without hiding the original information.

# TABLES

SIS likely contains many tables, so create a consistent table design.

Improve:

- header styling
- row spacing
- zebra differentiation if appropriate
- hover state
- borders
- alignment
- numeric alignment
- empty states
- responsive overflow
- sticky table headers where useful

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT globally apply destructive CSS such as:

table *
div *
span *
input *

without proper scope.

Some old portals rely heavily on tables for layout, so distinguish between:

DATA TABLES

and

LAYOUT TABLES

before modifying them.

# FORMS

Improve:

- inputs
- selects
- textareas
- radio buttons
- checkboxes
- labels
- validation messages
- submit buttons
- disabled states

But preserve:

- names
- IDs
- values
- event listeners
- form submission behavior
- validation logic

Never replace functional form elements just for appearance when CSS styling is sufficient.

# INFORMATION REORGANIZATION

You may reorganize information when it produces a meaningful usability improvement.

Examples:

Bad:

Attendance buried several clicks deep.

Better:

Dashboard card:
"Attendance: 86% — View Details"

Bad:

Today's timetable hidden inside the complete timetable.

Better:

Dashboard:
"Today's Classes"

Bad:

CGPA hidden inside a large results table.

Better:

CGPA summary card + original results page.

However:

Do NOT duplicate huge amounts of information.

Use summaries that link to the original detailed pages.

# QUICK ACTIONS

If useful based on the real SIS navigation, add a compact Quick Actions section.

For example:

- Attendance
- Timetable
- Results
- Course Registration
- Fee Details
- Profile

Use the portal's REAL URLs/actions.

Do not hard-code routes until verified.

# EXTENSION CONTROLS

Add a small unobtrusive extension control accessible while using SIS.

Possible options:

Enhanced UI: ON/OFF

Theme:
- Light
- Dark
- System

Optional:
- Compact mode
- Reduced motion

The user must always be able to disable the redesign and instantly return to the original SIS presentation.

This is extremely important.

# ORIGINAL PORTAL FALLBACK

Provide an easy way to temporarily disable enhancements.

Example:

Enhanced SIS
[ ON ]

When OFF:

- remove extension-added classes
- remove injected enhancement components
- restore original presentation
- do NOT require page reload if technically reasonable

Never prevent students from accessing the original portal.

# TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

Do NOT dump all logic into one content script.

Create a maintainable portal enhancement architecture.

Adapt it to the existing repository, but conceptually something like:

src/
  sis/
    selectors/
    parsers/
    observers/
    routes/
    enhancement/

  features/
    theme/
    dashboard/
    attendance/
    timetable/
    results/
    navigation/

  styles/
    tokens.css
    light.css
    dark.css
    components.css
    tables.css
    forms.css

  components/
    ThemeToggle
    QuickActions
    SummaryCard
    EnhancementControls

Do not create unnecessary abstractions if the extension is currently small.

Keep it proportional to the project.

# PORTAL ADAPTER

Centralize SIS-specific selectors.

Avoid scattering things like:

document.querySelector("#some-random-id")

through dozens of files.

Prefer something conceptually like:

sisSelectors.dashboard.studentName
sisSelectors.dashboard.cgpa
sisSelectors.attendance.table
sisSelectors.navigation.sidebar

This makes future SIS changes much easier to repair.

# DOM PARSING

When extracting portal information:

1. Read existing DOM.
2. Normalize it.
3. Render enhancement UI from normalized data.

Conceptually:

SIS DOM
    ↓
Portal parser
    ↓
Normalized student data
    ↓
Enhanced UI

Example normalized structure:

{
  student: {},
  semester: {},
  courses: [],
  attendance: [],
  timetable: [],
  results: []
}

Only include fields actually obtainable from SIS.

# DYNAMIC CONTENT

SIS may dynamically replace portions of the DOM.

Handle this safely.

Use MutationObserver where needed, but:

- do not observe the entire DOM with expensive callbacks unless necessary
- debounce expensive operations
- disconnect observers when unnecessary
- prevent duplicate enhancement initialization

Use a marker such as:

data-sis-enhanced="true"

to avoid enhancing the same component repeatedly.

# CSS SAFETY

Avoid destructive global rules.

BAD:

div {
  background: #111 !important;
}

table {
  display: block !important;
}

* {
  color: white !important;
}

GOOD:

body.sis-enhanced .verified-selector {
   ...
}

Scope enhancement styles carefully.

Use !important only when overriding legacy SIS styles genuinely requires it.

Do not turn the stylesheet into thousands of uncontrolled !important declarations.

# EXTENSION UI ISOLATION

For extension-created floating controls/panels, consider Shadow DOM if it improves isolation from SIS styles.

Portal-reskin CSS itself can target verified SIS components normally.

# PERFORMANCE

The extension must remain lightweight.

Avoid:

- large UI libraries unless already present
- unnecessary runtime dependencies
- continuous DOM polling
- expensive MutationObservers
- repeated layout measurements
- unnecessary animations
- excessive blur/backdrop-filter
- large bundled assets

Page interaction should remain as fast as the original portal.

# SECURITY AND PRIVACY — VERY IMPORTANT

This is a university portal containing private student information.

The enhancement must be designed privacy-first.

DO NOT:

- collect passwords
- read login passwords
- send session cookies anywhere
- upload student information
- upload grades
- upload attendance
- upload student IDs
- upload portal HTML
- perform analytics on private academic information
- transmit SIS data to an external backend
- interfere with authentication
- modify authentication cookies
- bypass authorization
- attempt to expose hidden information

All UI enhancement and SIS parsing should happen locally in the browser.

Use the minimum Chrome permissions necessary.

Ideally limit host permissions to:

https://lhr-sis.comsats.edu.pk/*

Do not request <all_urls> merely for this feature.

Do not intercept unrelated browsing traffic.

# AUTHENTICATION

The extension does NOT provide authentication.

Students should:

1. Navigate to the real SIS.
2. Log in normally.
3. SIS authenticates them.
4. The extension enhances the authenticated UI.

Do not duplicate or proxy the SIS login form.

Do not store university credentials.

# DATA INTEGRITY

Never change actual SIS academic information.

The extension is a presentation layer.

If calculations such as percentages are added:

- derive them only from reliable displayed values
- isolate the calculation logic
- handle missing values
- handle malformed values
- never replace authoritative SIS values with calculated values

# ERROR HANDLING

If a selector stops matching because SIS changes its website:

DO NOT break the page.

Instead:

- gracefully skip that enhancement
- preserve original UI
- log a useful development warning
- allow other enhancements to continue functioning

The enhancement should fail component-by-component rather than taking down the entire page.

# RESPONSIVENESS

Although SIS is primarily desktop-oriented, improve responsiveness where reasonably possible.

Support typical laptop resolutions particularly well:

1366x768
1440x900
1920x1080

Do not force mobile layouts if doing so would break legacy SIS functionality.

# ACCESSIBILITY

Improve:

- contrast
- focus indicators
- clickable areas
- form label clarity
- keyboard navigation
- semantic extension-created controls

Respect:

prefers-reduced-motion

Do not communicate important states solely through color.

# ANIMATIONS

Keep animations extremely subtle.

Allowed:

- small hover transitions
- sidebar transitions
- theme transition
- card appearance
- dropdown transitions

Avoid:

- page entrance animations everywhere
- scroll animations
- parallax
- large motion effects
- distracting glowing effects

This is a productivity/student portal.

# IMPORTANT PRODUCT PRINCIPLE

Do not redesign something merely because you can.

For every structural change ask:

"Does this make SIS faster or easier for a student to use?"

If not, leave the original structure intact and simply improve its visual styling.

# IMPLEMENTATION PRIORITY

Prioritize in this order:

PHASE 1
- architecture integration
- extension enable/disable
- theme system
- design tokens
- global typography/background
- navigation
- cards
- forms
- buttons
- tables

PHASE 2
- dashboard summaries
- quick actions
- attendance improvements
- timetable improvements
- results improvements

PHASE 3
- polish
- responsive fixes
- accessibility
- edge cases
- dynamic DOM handling
- performance optimization

# TESTING

Test every important SIS section you can access.

Verify:

- login page remains functional
- authenticated dashboard works
- links still work
- logout still works
- forms still submit
- selects still work
- buttons remain clickable
- tables retain all information
- navigation functions normally
- extension does not create duplicated components
- dark mode covers all important surfaces
- light mode still looks correct
- enhancement can be disabled
- refreshing retains user preferences
- page transitions retain enhancements
- no obvious console errors
- no significant layout shifts
- no horizontal overflow introduced
- no student data leaves the browser

# FINAL POLISH

After implementation, perform a complete visual audit.

Look for:

- inconsistent border radius
- mismatched spacing
- bad text contrast
- white elements in dark mode
- broken table rows
- legacy colors bleeding through
- misaligned icons
- inconsistent buttons
- cramped forms
- horizontal overflow
- duplicated borders
- excessively large headings
- inconsistent hover states
- broken responsive areas
- extension UI conflicting with SIS CSS

Fix these issues instead of stopping at "functionally complete."

# FINAL RESULT

The end result should make a COMSATS Lahore student immediately feel:

"This is still my SIS portal, but it looks and works dramatically better."

The extension should enhance the existing experience rather than fighting against it.

Most importantly:

PRESERVE EXISTING EXTENSION FUNCTIONALITY.
PRESERVE SIS FUNCTIONALITY.
DO NOT TOUCH AUTHENTICATION/CREDENTIALS.
KEEP STUDENT DATA LOCAL.
USE VERIFIED DOM SELECTORS.
IMPLEMENT GRACEFUL FALLBACKS.
MAKE THE UI ACTUALLY MORE USEFUL, NOT JUST PRETTIER.

Begin by auditing the repository and current SIS DOM, then implement the feature completely and test it across the available SIS sections.
